Changelog

Mirrored from libs/mix/CHANGELOG.md, where releases update it. The component's page is mix. This page describes the current main branch of MixOS.

Unreleased

Added

  • analyzer::Analysis.functions reports named function declarations with name, file and line, including nested and duplicate definitions but excluding quoted and remote source. mix lint --json and --data expose this list in schema 3; every existing key and diagnostic retains its meaning.

  • mix lint reads in-file pragmas: -- lint: globals a, b declares injected names, -- lint: ignore CODE suppresses CODE on the next line holding code (or on its own line when written after code) and -- lint: ignore-file CODE suppresses it file-wide. A bare or unknown pragma is MIX-E1601; a suppression that matches nothing is the note MIX-D3019. An ssh_mix body reads its own pragmas.

  • MIX-W2312: a bareword null, None, undefined, NULL or nullptr used as a value is the string "null"; the warning carries a quick fix to nil where the word is surely a value. mix lint --fix applies quick fixes; --json reports each as fix. Diagnostic gains a fix field.

  • MIX-W2313: a function named after one of the mix binary's shell extensions (ai, ai_diagnose, context). Lint now knows those extensions (MIX_SHELL_EXTENSIONS, AnalyzerConfig::extensions), so calling one is no longer MIX-E1102.

  • MIX-W2314 / MIX-W2315: member calls into a module bound once to a literal require() path are checked against its exports, for arity and for a missing name. Warnings in this release, while the check is new.

  • The parser names the fix for let i = 0, var/const, and a bareword i = … ("Mix has no let: write $i = …").

  • Add the archive feature with the tar_list, tar_unpack and tar_pack builtins. Archives use zstd (default), gzip or no codec. tar_unpack validates every member, extracts into a staging directory and renames it into place only after the stream verifies. See mix man tar.

  • Harden archive builtins: count trailing padding against the shared decoded stream budget, reject oversized declared files before creation and bound copying, cap GNU/PAX metadata payloads before buffering, and refuse unread gzip input or additional members. Packing captures capabilities only with keep_special_bits:true and walks pinned directory/file descriptors without following replacement symlinks. Rollback restores directory access and reports cleanup failures. Empty/truncated zstd headers now raise ARCHIVE_STREAM_CORRUPT. GNU sparse entries are refused; tar_list also accepts max_entries. Each fix has targeted archive regression coverage.

  • Archive review fixes. tar_unpack restores only user.* xattrs by default: security.capability needs keep_special_bits:true, and trusted.*, POSIX ACLs (system.*) and the rest of security.* need the new privileged_xattrs:true. Retained xattr bytes are bounded across the archive by the new max_xattr_bytes (16 MiB). Staging has an unpredictable name and is held by descriptor; members are created one O_NOFOLLOW component at a time relative to it, and the commit refuses to replace anything that appeared at dest (RENAME_NOREPLACE). Owner, mode and mtime failures are no longer discarded: an owner that cannot be applied is listed in the receipt's new warnings, and then its setuid/setgid bits and capability are dropped; mode and mtime failures raise. PAX global headers (git archive) are accepted as metadata (receipt metadata, list kind "metadata"). A bare relative dest or output name means the current directory. tar_pack refuses an output inside its source and raises when a file changes size while it is packed.

  • Archive review, round 2. tar_unpack refuses a dest parent that another user could write (group/other-writable without the sticky bit, or owned by neither the caller nor root) before creating anything, and checks the new staging directory is the caller's, 0700 and empty. Without RENAME_NOREPLACE the commit now fails closed and rolls back. Implicitly created parent directories count against max_entries (receipt implicit_dirs). zstd content checksums are verified on unpack and list, and tar_pack now writes one.

  • analyzer::Analysis carries handlers: one HandlerDeclaration (command, file, line) per on <command> statement in the parsed AST, in source order, with duplicates kept. analyze() collects them with the existing statement walker. Remote ssh_mix bodies are not included. mix lint --json and --data report the same list as an additive handlers field. The data is structural: it does not prove that a handler runs or is reachable.

  • mix_tokens(source[, {comments: true}]) returns the real lexer's token stream as [{kind, text, line, col}], with the exact source text of each token and, on request, the # and -- comments. A tool that reads Mix source no longer re-derives the grammar. Source that does not lex raises MIX_SOURCE_LEX with details {line, col}. Backed by the new Lexer::source_tokens. See mix man syntax.

  • fsync(path[, {recursive}]) makes a file, a directory (its entries, after a rename or remove) or a whole tree durable, without sync -f's flush of the whole filesystem. It returns the number of inodes synced; a failure raises FSYNC_FAILED naming the path.

  • dns_query(name, type[, {server, port, timeout, tcp, recurse}]) asks one DNS server one question and returns the rcode, the aa/ra/tc flags and every section with TTLs. Timeouts and unreachable servers come back as {ok: false, error_code}. It is the new dns feature (hickory-proto, the version mail-auth already uses); the mix binary turns it on.

  • walk(dir, {strict: true}) raises WALK_UNREADABLE, naming the first directory it cannot read or entry it cannot stat, instead of skipping it.

  • chown(path, uid, gid, {follow_symlinks: false}) changes a symlink itself (lchown).

  • flock and fcntl_lock take create: false, which refuses a missing lock file with LOCK_FILE_MISSING and creates nothing.

  • tar_unpack and tar_list accept GNU tar's ./ member prefix (tar -C dir .); a ./ directory entry's metadata is applied to dest. Relative symlinks may climb with leading .. while they stay inside dest, judged from the link's own directory (demo/lib/alias -> ../bin/demo). Gzip input may have several members, as pigz and cat a.gz b.gz write.

  • mix man sqlopen documents the SQLite builtins and their modes.

Changed

  • tar_unpack's numeric_owner now defaults to true only for root, as GNU tar does. An ordinary user's unpacked files keep their own uid and gid; a non-root chown could still give a file any of the caller's groups. Pass numeric_owner: true for the old behaviour. A setuid/setgid bit or capability is now kept only where the file ends up with the owner the archive named, also when owners are not restored.

  • A symlink target may no longer pass through another symlink the archive creates, in either order, and .. may only lead a target: a/../b is refused.

  • A shared flock or fcntl_lock opens an existing file read-only, so it no longer needs write access to the lock file.

  • sqlopen raises OPTION_INVALID for a mode other than "ro", "rw" or "rwc" ("rwc" is new: read-write, creating the file, the same as "rw"). An unknown mode used to open read-only, so "rwc" could not create a database. A read-only open of a missing file raises SQL_NO_DATABASE naming "rwc".

  • A member call $m.name(...) on a map holding a function member calls that member in every mode, --serve included; an extension (the shell's context()) no longer wins there.

  • MIX-W2304 names the result shape and suggests the field a bash, Python or Node spelling means (code, rc, status → exit_code).

  • The default remote mix binary is now /opt/mixos/bin/mix (was the legacy install path's mix). It applies to ssh_mix, ssh_mix_many, ssh_exec, ssh_run's env_transport: "mix" and send_mail's host hop whenever neither mix_bin nor MIX_REMOTE_BIN is set. For a host still on the old install path, pass mix_bin or set MIX_REMOTE_BIN to its mix.

Fixed

  • A send after a failed Bus connection retries within its timeout, re-reading MIXOS_NODED_URL and node configuration. A stale probe cannot replace a newer connection, and reconnecting does not hold the state lock.
  • SIGINT still ends a non-interactive evaluation when a catch keeps computing: after a cleanup grace the interrupt becomes standing. Nested catches and finally control flow cannot swallow it. A served citizen keeps its graceful deregistration and exit status 0.
  • read_file, write_file and append_file yield while waiting on a FIFO, so served citizens still answer other verbs and QUIT. Reads honour the string limit, and the FIFO path keeps the normal builtin arity rules.
  • fs_watch recovery (after a lost or overflowed event stream) re-arms each directory watch in place instead of unwatching and watching it again, so a change that lands during the repair (the close-write of a save racing the overflow) is still reported.
  • mix lint no longer reports MIX-E1101 for a variable assigned in a piped statement ($v = 1 | cat).
  • mix lint MIX-W2307 (send result never checked) now counts a status read inside an if condition, a map value, a nested call argument or a string interpolation. A correctly checked send no longer warns.
  • MIX-W2307 treats every writer of $rc, $result and $reply as an overwrite: publish(), sh, $(...), pipes to external commands, user assignments, address-block calls and calls to functions that send. A send followed by one of these, and no read before it, now warns.
  • MIX-W2307 is conservative by construction: a construct whose effect on the status the analyser cannot prove absent counts as an overwrite. A call is proven non-writing only for a function defined in the file whose body and parameter defaults do not write, or for one of the pure builtins (no I/O, process, bus, network, clock or function-valued argument). Any other builtin, value call ($f()), method call, include or source, and any name defined nowhere in the file, now overwrites. A name that is also bound as a variable or parameter is a barrier, because a callable binding runs before a named function. A bare word that names a function is a call. A function that can exit, panic, die or fail uncaught ends its caller's path, so a read after that call does not discharge a send. String and heredoc ${...} fallbacks (${x ?? sh "..."}) are analysed as the program they are, and an index is evaluated before its object. This can add warnings for code that is correct but calls a non-pure builtin between a send and its check.

0.116.0

Added

  • The remote mix binary is configurable. Every builtin that drives a remote mix (ssh_mix, ssh_mix_many, ssh_exec, ssh_run's env_transport: "mix", send_mail's host hop) resolves it in one place: the mix_bin option, else the local env var MIX_REMOTE_BIN (empty counts as unset), else the old install path's mix, the unchanged default. The value is interpolated into the remote command string, so it must be an absolute path or a bare name using only [A-Za-z0-9_./+-]; anything else raises OPTION_INVALID locally before ssh runs. A host with mix only at /opt/mixos/bin/mix used to fail with exit 127.

Changed

  • ssh_exec's remote_mix option is now validated the same way (it was interpolated unchecked) and is an alias of mix_bin; passing both raises.

0.115.0

Added

  • unix_connect(path[, {timeout, frame}]): a client for a local unix-domain stream socket, in tcp_connect's handle space, so tcp_send, tcp_recv, tcp_recv_line, tcp_on and tcp_close take it. The connect is bounded by timeout and fails at once on a full backlog (UNIX_CONNECT_BUSY). frame: "nul" makes a line a NUL-terminated frame, the framing of systemd's Varlink services and of hostd, for tcp_recv_line and tcp_on {frame: "line"} alike. Refusals carry UNIX_CONNECT_* codes. mix man system documents it.

Changed

  • One frame splitter serves tcp_recv_line (blocking and Class C) and tcp_on line mode, keyed to the connection's delimiter. One trailing CR is still stripped from an LF line.

Fixed

  • max now caps a complete line too. A line longer than max whose terminator arrived in the same read used to be delivered, so whether it was refused depended on packet timing. All three paths (tcp_recv_line blocking and Class C, tcp_on line mode) now refuse it the same way.

0.114.0

Changed

  • Released with mix-shell 0.114.0, whose usage-statistics store is now an append-only JSONL store (mix man stats). The language and its builtins are unchanged.

0.113.1

Fixed

  • An on header reads a hyphenated name whole, like a send target: on dopus-test.command.executed handles that topic. Before, the header stopped at the hyphen, so the handler registered as dopus with -test.command.executed as its body: it parsed, linted clean and never fired. Leading-zero segments (on svc-01.ping) lex as part of the name, as they do after send.

0.113.0

Added

  • mime_type(path[, {content}]): a file's type from the freedesktop shared-mime-info database, decided by GLib's rules, so it agrees with gio info and the file manager (checked against GIO on 5,047 files). Returns {mime, by, uncertain, exists, parents}. Behind the new mime feature, through the new mimedb crate. mix man io documents it.

0.112.1

Added

  • tcp_send(handle, payload[, {timeout}]): one deadline bounds the whole send, however many partial writes a slow reader forces (seconds, 0 = wait forever). On expiry it raises TCP_SEND_TIMEOUT with details: {written, total} and retires the handle; bytes already written stay written. The wait honours SIGTERM and Ctrl-C. On a tcp_on handle the timeout is the receipt deadline. Without the option tcp_send is unchanged.

Fixed

  • SIGTERM now ends a blocking tcp_accept, tcp_recv, tcp_recv_line or ws_recv at once, as it ends sleep(). On unix these numeric waits now wait on the async runtime instead of blocking the evaluator's thread, so the shell's SIGTERM and Ctrl-C handling can cancel them. Before, a script looping on tcp_accept($l, {timeout: 0.05}) ignored SIGTERM until the 15 s backstop forced it out. Options, results and error messages are unchanged.
  • A receive returns data already buffered before it judges the deadline, so a very short timeout no longer returns nil while a line sits in the buffer. Traffic that delivers nothing (a WebSocket Pong flood, a line trickled with no newline) now counts against the deadline and the interrupt flag, so a finite timeout ends on time and SIGTERM still ends an untimed wait.
  • A very large receive timeout in a Class C tcp_recv/ws_recv waits forever instead of overflowing the deadline.

0.112.0

Added

  • Server-side TCP. tcp_listen(host, port[, {backlog}]) binds and listens and returns a listener handle; host is required ("127.0.0.1" is the normal choice) and port 0 takes an ephemeral port. tcp_local_addr(handle) returns {host, port} for a listener or connection. tcp_accept(listener[, {timeout}]) returns an ordinary connected handle, or nil on timeout; in a Class C body it waits on native readiness. tcp_on on a listener delivers one accepted: {handle, peer} event per connection, and tcp_accept(source) reads that source outside serve mode. tcp_close closes a listener. Listeners and the connections they accept belong to the evaluator generation and close when it retires. Errors carry stable codes (TCP_LISTEN_ADDR_IN_USE, TCP_LISTEN_PERMISSION, TCP_LISTEN_ADDR_UNAVAILABLE, TCP_LISTEN_ADDRESS, TCP_LISTEN_ARGUMENT, TCP_ACCEPT_HANDLE, TCP_HANDLE_LIMIT, TCP_LISTENER).
  • The handle limit is server-side: at most 1024 listeners and accepted connections are live at once, each holding a slot until it closes, and tcp_listen and tcp_accept refuse with TCP_HANDLE_LIMIT past it. tcp_connect is not limited and behaves as before.
  • A blocking tcp_accept wakes promptly on Ctrl-C through a SIGINT wake socket that interrupt::init installs, and rechecks the interrupt flag at least every 250 ms, so no waiter misses it.
  • on @.verb registers a handler under the serve name: the unquoted @ is replaced by the --serve name (the value serve_name() returns) when the handler registers, so one generic script run as --name photo answers photo.verb and a second instance as --name other answers other.verb. Dispatch, HELP and handler listings show the resolved name; the AST keeps @.verb. Outside mix --serve the statement raises SERVE_PREFIX_OUTSIDE_SERVE. Each segment after @. must be a bare name, quoted or not. on a.@.b, on @, on @x.y, a quoted on "@.x", a quoted segment that isn't a bare name (on @."a.b") and @ in an expression are parse errors (an unquoted @ was a lexer error before). Positions that read raw source text now accept @ as an ordinary character where it used to fail lexing: a bareword source/include path (source ./foo@bar.mix) and the command after | (print(1) | cat @foo).

Fixed

  • HTTP 1xx, 204 and 304 responses are bodyless on every method, not only HEAD. A conditional GET answered 304 with Content-Encoding: gzip no longer fails with HTTP_BODY, so ETag polling works.

0.111.0

Added

  • script_path() returns the entry script's absolute, symlink-resolved path, the same answer as realpath($0), fixed when the script starts (a later chdir(), including one in the prelude, does not move it). It is nil under mix -c, in the REPL, for mix - and when the path cannot be resolved at start. A required module, even during its top-level init, gets the entry script's path.

Fixed

  • Lambdas created inside a served on handler keep the handler's local variables when they run later (they faulted with undefined variable). A module first required inside a handler still reads its globals live.
  • password_hash sha512-crypt output is now verifiable by glibc crypt(3) and Dovecot.
  • chr() and ord() structured error codes are pinned by tests.

0.109.1

Initial MixOS transplant of the current language library and regression corpus. Language syntax, builtin contracts and evaluator behaviour retain the source version. Environment and project roots use MixOS names. SSH helpers retain the installed Mix path used by existing predecessor nodes during the migration.
